The image shows a corn ear with its husks pulled back, revealing the interior completely replaced by a large, dark brown-to-black mass of spores. Key features:

- Entire ear structure replaced by dark spore mass (not a discrete gall on one part)
- Dark brown/black powdery teliospores filling the husk cavity
- Stringy vascular bundle strands visible within the spore mass
- Husks appear bleached/tan-yellow
- No normal kernel development visible

This matches **Head_Smut** precisely: the entire ear is replaced by a teliospore mass, with intact vascular bundle threads giving a stringy appearance (the key differentiator from Common Smut). Common Smut produces discrete galls on various plant parts, while Head Smut replaces the whole ear or tassel with a spore-filled gall covered initially by a white membrane (now ruptured here).
